html:
The Ecuadorian and Peruvian War was a short border war in July 1941, in which Peru invaded southern Ecuador. In the Rio Protocol of January 1942 Ecuador gave up its claims to a large part of the Amazon.

The two countries had argued since independence over their border in the lowlands, a legacy of vague colonial lines. Peru's army was larger and better armed, and it occupied the province of El Oro on the coast. With the world at war, the United States and other countries pressed Ecuador to sign quickly.

Ecuadorians saw the treaty as a national humiliation, and later governments rejected it. Fighting flared again in 1981 and in the Cenepa War of 1995. A final peace treaty was signed in Brasília in 1998. The war left Ecuador with a lasting sense of having lost much of its Amazon to Peru.
sum: The Ecuadorian and Peruvian War was a short border war in July 1941, in which Peru invaded southern Ecuador. In the Rio Protocol of January 1942 Ecuador gave up its claims to a large part of the Amazon.
